name: Storm hysteresis index
title: In a fails spike, does repo stress come before or after?
what: Plots one series against another through each stress episode; the loop's direction says which peaked first, scored −1 to 1.
pick_line: A calendar-locked null (shift by whole quarters) to test whether any loop survives quarter-end timing.
data: Public aggregates (NY Fed fails, OFR repo, CFTC TFF); descriptive only
one: In fails spikes the repo spread peaks after fails, but mostly because storms end at quarter-ends.

picture.la: Usual tool: one symmetric, same-week link (r = −0.43)

findings.h: The repo spread runs anticlockwise through fails storms: it peaks after fails.
findings.t: Across 13 financing-fails storms (peaks 2019-09 to 2026-04), the DVP minus tri-party overnight spread has mean hysteresis index −0.17: 6 storms at or below −0.2, none at or above +0.2. Circular-shift null (4,999): p = 0.042; Holm over the three pre-registered series: 0.126, so not a pre-registered finding. Dropping any one storm leaves the mean between −0.20 and −0.14.
findings.note: Usual tools see one symmetric, near-simultaneous link: correlation of log fails with the spread −0.43 in the same week; ARDL picks spread lags 0–2 with mixed signs, and the reverse ARDL picks only the same week.

findings.h: Most of the loop is quarter-end timing.
findings.t: Post hoc (not pre-registered): masking the 44 quarter-end and year-end weeks and interpolating the spread through them shrinks the mean index to −0.08 (p = 0.35); 4 storms stay at or below −0.2. Several storms end in late December or early October, where the spread jumps for balance-sheet reasons.
findings.note: So the loop shape is real in the data, but the reason is largely the calendar, not fails driving repo stress. The top pick tests this properly.

chart.la: Mean index vs null, three series

findings.h: DVP volume and leveraged-fund positioning show no loop.
findings.t: DVP outstanding: mean index −0.14, p = 0.20 (Holm 0.40), though its flushing index is +0.45 (volume rises into the fails peak). Leveraged-fund net short (11 storms to 2025-12): +0.03, p = 0.75. Daily repo-only storms (21 spread spikes, 2018-05 to 2026-06) against DVP volume: −0.06, p = 0.33.
findings.note: Power check: 13 idealised weekly storms with a one-week lag are detected every time (200 of 200); with no lag, 7% false alarms. Weekly sampling is not what limits it; the storms differ from each other.

chart.title: Size of mean hysteresis index (sign in label; 0 = no loop)

findings.h: A rising-limb term does not improve forecasts.
findings.t: Walk-forward 1-week-ahead log fails, 221 weeks (2022-07-06 to 2026-09-23), training from 2018: ARDL RMSE 0.2607; ARDL plus spread × rising-limb term 0.2619 (+0.5%, Diebold–Mariano p = 0.25; pre-set bar −3% and p < 0.10); SARIMAX(1,0,1) with lagged spread 0.2582; random walk 0.2934.
findings.note: Low priority (forecasting), reported because it was pre-registered.
